question: For Warrant 1 Condition A with at least two major-street lanes and one minor-street lane, what volumes must exist and over what time basis, and does meeting them compel signal installation?
model_answer: Direct Answer: For Warrant 1 Condition A, the volumes given in both of the 100 percent columns of Condition A in Table 4C-1 must exist on the major street and the more critical minor-street approach for each of any 8 hours of an average day, with major- and minor-street volumes counted for the same 8 hours. The evidence provided contains only the table's headings, not the specific numeric thresholds for the two-major-lane/one-minor-lane row, so those exact numbers cannot be quoted here. Importantly, meeting the warrant does not compel installation: the MUTCD says only that the need for a signal "should be considered" (Guidance, not a Standard). Standards (mandatory): - "These major-street and minor-street volumes shall be for the same 8 hours for each condition; however, the 8 hours that are selected for the Condition A analysis shall not be required to be the same 8 hours that are selected for the Condition B analysis." - "These major-street and minor-street volumes shall be for the same 8 hours for each condition; however, the 8 hours satisfied in Condition A shall not be required to be the same 8 hours satisfied in Condition B." Guidance (recommended): - "The need for a traffic control signal should be considered if an engineering study finds that one of the following conditions exist for each of any 8 hours of an average day: A. The vehicles per hour given in both of the 100 percent columns of Condition A in Table 4C-1 exist on the major street and the more critical minor-street approach, respectively, to the intersection..." — this "should be considered" wording means warrant satisfaction does not mandate signal installation. - Alternatively, the warrant may be considered satisfied at reduced (80 percent) volume levels if both Condition A and Condition B are met at the 80 percent columns for each of any 8 hours of an average day. Options (permitted): - "Any four consecutive 15-minute periods may be considered as 1 hour if the separate 1-hour periods used in the warrant analysis do not overlap each other and both the major-street volume and the minor-street volume are for the same specific 1-hour periods." Citations: - Section 4C.02 Standard §5 (p.653) - Section 4C.02 Standard §10 (p.654) - Section 4C.02 Guidance §4 (p.653) - Section 4C.02 Guidance §9 (p.654) - Section 4C.01 Option §15 (p.652)
gold_answer: For each of the same 8 selected hours, 600 vph must exist on the major street (both approaches total) and 150 vph on the critical minor approach (one direction) at the 100-percent thresholds. Meeting the warrant does not compel installation; an engineering study must determine whether a signal is justified.
